bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (bifrost_app::accessory_access), springboard/core/src/accessory_manager.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_descriptors.rs; related: springboard/src/bare/input.rs (evdev device discovery), springboard/src/bare/docbroker.rs (file grants), springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (permission manifest)
summary: Accessory Access is a USB-only framework: listeners match connected USB accessories and receive attach and detach events. BifrOSt now has the full path: the shell reads the bus, an app that declares the usb permission asks the person for one device (filters built from the same matching criteria), receives attach and detach events for devices it was granted, and opens them through the shell, which keeps the device node out of the sandbox. A hardware check on Midget remains.

features.note: AccessoryManager::sync takes a full bus snapshot, detaches what is missing, attaches what is new and reports the connection ids it changed; apps reach the manager through the SDK module, and both behaviours are tested headless. Gap: no bus source feeds sync with real enumeration yet, which needs hardware and a lab check on Midget. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): AccessoryManager::sync is now fed by the shell: the usb service calls usb_bus_source::poll every second, and what attached or detached becomes the events apps receive. Apps reach it through usb_access (request, devices, events), not a manager of their own. Midget check: cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::the_scan_lists_usb_and_hid_devices_but_never_protected_ones; on the device: plug and unplug a USB device and read the usb service's connected and disconnected events.

The device descriptors, configuration and strings are public fields, and a detached accessory keeps its identity record, tested headless in core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: no bus source fills the strings and configuration yet, which needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): usb_access::Device carries the id, name, vendor, product, device class and interface classes of a granted accessory; open returns the configuration, interfaces and endpoints. Strings beyond the product name are not read. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::devices_and_requests_replies_decode, an_open_reply_decodes_for_usb_and_hid).

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (MatchingCriteria, DeviceMatch, InterfaceMatch), springboard/core/src/usb_descriptors.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_grants.rs
features.note: Criteria select by vendor, product, class, subclass and protocol, and by interface; a device with no configuration read does not match an interface criterion, tested in core/tests and sdk/tests parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: the criteria can only be checked against descriptors the caller has read, which needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): usb_access::filters_from_criteria turns MatchingCriteria into the filters of request (vendor, product, device class, one filter per interface criterion with its class). Subclass and protocol cannot be expressed in a filter; the app reads them from the open reply. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::matching_criteria_become_filters_one_per_interface_criterion).

Events are queued per listener key, a detach reaches only the listeners told of the attach, and sync produces them from a snapshot; all tested headless in core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: no hotplug source on a real bus feeds them yet, which needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): The hotplug source is real: connected and disconnected events go to the apps that hold a grant for the device (an ungranted device is silent), and a handle closes with a closed event when the device is unplugged. Midget check: cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::a_granted_device_that_is_unplugged_loses_its_once_grant_and_tells_the_app; on the device: unplug a granted device.

features.feature: Kernel USB enumeration and system visibility
features.apple: IOUSBHost (underlies the framework, per the landing page)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (AccessoryManager, MatchingCriteria, attach and detach events); springboard/ui/src/device_browser.rs (USB device snapshots, add and remove events); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs:245 (binds /sys and /run/udev read-only into the app sandbox); springboard/src/installer/plan.rs:186 (raises the USB interrupt thread priority), springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_grants.rs
features.note: Apps match accessories by criteria and receive attach and detach events, and the device browser reports which USB devices came and went, both tested inline in their pure models. Gap: the sandbox binds no USB device nodes, so no app reaches a real accessory, and the shell supplies the bus snapshots. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): The shell enumerates /sys/bus/usb/devices and /sys/class/hidraw for the service; the sandbox still binds no USB device nodes on purpose (the shell is the broker), so the earlier gap is closed by design rather than by a bind. Midget check: cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: ssh midget and check that an app with the usb permission sees no /dev/bus/usb inside its sandbox while usb_access::open still works.

features.feature: Permission and access grant for USB devices
features.apple: Accessory Access authorization (accessory matching and listener registration)
features.note: Exclusive open by one owner, close only by that owner, and refusal of a disconnected accessory are modelled and tested headless. Gap: the permission manifest has no USB device permission and no prompt, so an app cannot request a grant yet, which needs the sandbox and hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Built: the usb and hid manifest permissions, the permission sheet (Allow Once, Always Allow, Don't Allow; Don't Allow is the default and an unanswered sheet grants nothing), grants per app and device with a cap of 32 per app, Always Allow saved in usb-app-grants.txt, Allow Once ended by app quit or unplug, a revoke switch under App Permissions, and an app asked once per run per device so it cannot nag. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; Settings > Privacy & Security > App Permissions shows a USB AND HID DEVICES group (screenshot with `bifrost pc midget screen`); turn the switch off and the app's open handles close.

Error values have readable messages and are exposed to apps; the open and state messages are checked in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs and core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Not yet verified on Midget. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Done events class a failure (denied, timeout, stall, disconnected, busy, overflow, other) with the message; the exclusive-open errors of the manager are unchanged. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::a_done_event_carries_data_a_count_or_an_error).

gaps: No bus source calls attach and detach for USB accessories, so no app receives real hotplug events yet.
No USB device permission in the app permission manifest (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs), and no grant flow comparable to docbroker.rs for USB.
The accessory object's descriptors come from the caller; nothing reads them from a device.
No USB device nodes are bound into the app sandbox, so a listener cannot match a real accessory from an app.
